title: Latency telemetry hedging and noise-aware SLO runbook
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Reduce noisy pager storms and improve SLO signal fidelity by implementing a hedging layer for latency telemetry, augmenting trace hooks with contextual sampling, and codifying a noise-aware SLO runbook. This ticket covers design, prototype, and rollout for a platform-level mitigation that sits between ingest and alerting.

Background: We are seeing frequent burn-rate alerts triggered by short-lived spikes (e.g., GC pauses, noisy downstream calls) that do not indicate systemic regressions. On-call overhead is increasing and teams are losing signal trust. Current trace sampling is coarse and we lack a lightweight pre-aggregation step that separates transient spikes from sustained degradations.

Scope:
- Implement a hedging aggregator that computes short-window and medium-window latency distributions per route/model.
- Add trace-hook enrichment to annotate requests with upstream-cause tags (cache-miss, db-retry, large-payload) to support attribution.
- Introduce a noise detector that uses histogram smoothing + change-point heuristics to mark bursts as transient and suppress burn-rate escalation until sustained.
- Ship a draft runbook that defines paging thresholds, quiet-window rules, and a manual override for customer-impacting incidents.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Accuracy vs cost: The hedging aggregator will maintain lightweight sketches (t-digest) instead of full histograms to keep memory down; we accept slight quantile error in exchange for low ingestion cost.
- Latency of detection: Using two windows (30s short, 10m medium) gives quicker detection without overreacting; can add adaptive windowing later.
- Attribution quality: Trace-hook enrichment will prioritize high-precision tags (error codes, retry counts) to avoid false attribution; some causes (e.g., noisy network) may remain ambiguous.
- Failure modes: If the hedging layer fails, alerts should fall back to existing burn-rate rules. The system must be observable (L0 metrics) and have an automated fail-open policy.

Acceptance criteria:
- Deployed hedging aggregator in staging with per-route short/medium quantiles visible in Console.
- Trace hooks annotated on >95% of sampled requests in staging.
- Noise detector reduces actionable burn-rate alerts by >=40% on historical noisy traces (backtest).
- Runbook published in Confluence (link in comments) and reviewed by SRE and PM.
- Rollout plan with gradual opt-in per team and feature flagging for hedging rules.

Rollout plan:
1) Prototype in telemetry lab and run backtests on last 30 days of traffic.
2) Staging deploy behind feature flag; expose metrics/dashboards to a pilot team.
3) Gradual opt-in: enable for low-risk teams, monitor metrics for 7 days, then expand.
4) Default on for non-customer-facing infra after validation.

Metrics to monitor post-rollout:
- Burn-rate alert frequency (per route)
- Pager escalations per week
- False-positive suppression rate (backtest-based estimate)
- Hedging aggregator error rate and resource usage
- Trace-hook enrichment coverage

Open questions:
- Which exact set of enrichment tags should be considered high-confidence for attribution? (suggestion: cache-miss, downstream-4xx, db-retry>1, large-body)
- Should teams be able to customize quiet-window length per route?
- What is the desired SLA for the hedging aggregator itself?
